note.text:
Weight is the force with which the Earth pulls a body. Its SI unit is the newton (N). It is measured with a spring balance (newton meter).
Weight = mass × g, where g is the pull on each kilogram. On Earth we use g = 10 N/kg, so a 5 kg bag weighs 5 × 10 = 50 N.
On the Moon, g is about 1.6 N/kg, so the same bag weighs much less, but its mass is still 5 kg.
Mass and weight are different:
• mass: quantity of matter, kilograms, beam balance, the same everywhere;
• weight: a force, newtons, spring balance, changes from place to place.

worked_example.problem: A tin of tomatoes has a mass of {m} g. What is its weight on Earth?
steps: Change the mass into kilograms: {m} g = {convertUnit(m, 'g', 'kg')} kg.

cards.idea: Weight is a force: the pull of the Earth on a body. It is measured in newtons (N) with a spring balance.
example: A bag of cement pulls down on your hands: that pull is its weight.

cards.idea: Weight = mass × g. On Earth, g = {g} N/kg.
On the Moon, g is smaller (about {gm} N/kg): weight is smaller, but the mass does not change.
example: A {m} kg bag weighs {weight(m, 10)} N on Earth and about {weight(m, gm)} N on the Moon. Its mass is {m} kg in both places.

check.prompt: An astronaut goes from the Earth to the Moon. What happens?

right.text: Her weight gets smaller, but her mass stays the same.

wrong.text: Her mass gets smaller, but her weight stays the same.
wrong.explain: Mass is the matter in her body: it does not change. The Moon pulls less, so her weight changes.

wrong.text: Both her mass and her weight stay the same.
wrong.explain: The Moon pulls less than the Earth, so her weight is smaller.

wrong.text: Her mass and weight both become zero.
wrong.explain: The Moon still pulls on her, and her body still has matter.

questions.prompt: Does each sentence describe mass or weight?

pool.left: the quantity of matter in a body
a force: the pull of gravity

questions.prompt: {cap(it)} has a mass of {m} kg. What is its weight on Earth? (g = {g} N/kg)

misconceptions.explain: That is the mass in kilograms. Weight = mass × g, in newtons.

questions.prompt: A packet of sugar has a mass of {m} g. What is its weight on Earth? (g = {g} N/kg)

misconceptions.explain: Change grams into kilograms first: g is in newtons per kilogram.

questions.hint: Change the grams into kilograms, then multiply by g.

questions.prompt: A spring balance shows that a sack of maize weighs {weight(m, g)} N. What is its mass? (g = {g} N/kg)

misconceptions.explain: To find the mass, divide the weight by g.

questions.prompt: An astronaut's tool bag has a mass of {m} kg. On the Moon, g is about {gm} N/kg. What does the bag weigh on the Moon?

misconceptions.explain: That is its weight on Earth. On the Moon use g = {gm} N/kg.
That is the mass. Weight = mass × g.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: Mass is the same on the Moon as on Earth.

wrong.explain: Weight is a force, measured in newtons (N). Kilograms measure mass.

wrong.text: Mass is smaller on the Moon.
wrong.explain: Mass is the same everywhere. It is weight that is smaller on the Moon.
